_model: How a record's undated days and minutes spread over its first-to-last span. Fit 2026-11-12 on 28 multi-year game copies with dated activity (trophy/achievement/screenshot days): launch burst 80% (tau 120 days), end burst 10% (tau 14), floor 10%; held-out yearly error 0.35 vs 0.45 for spreading evenly. Minutes follow the modeled days (early_hours_boost 0). No day gets more than one play day. Implemented as fit first (Ronjan 2026-11-12); tuning comes after.
_model_overrides: Per game, on top of model. None yet (A Link Between Worlds tighter-window idea parked until the fitted model is reviewed)
_anchors: Known totals by a date, which the model must meet: before that date gets exactly this many minutes (and days, if given) and the model shapes the rest. Super Mario Maker Wii U: 84 h 10 min by 2015-12-18 (Ronjan's in-game stats, quoted in his 'Let's talk game of the year(s)!' post that day). A Link Between Worlds: half its days and time by the end of 2013 (Ronjan: beat it by then; a friend borrowed his 3DS and played it later).
_evidence: Real play days inside a record's span (Switch screenshot days) pull the model toward them: weight = prior_weight x model + one 14-day exponential kernel per real day, and real days count as played. Backtest 2026-11-12 (23 multi-year copies, hide part of each one's dated days, predict the rest's yearly split): with 1/2/4 known days, yearly error 0.31/0.28/0.28 vs 0.38/0.39/0.42 for the model alone; prior_weight 1 and a 14-day bandwidth were best at every count.
